query_text: Why do men have larger Adam's apples?

content.text:
Men typically have larger Adam’s apples because **testosterone during puberty causes the larynx — the “voice box” — to grow significantly**.

The Adam’s apple is the visible bump made by the **thyroid cartilage**, which sits at the front of the larynx. During puberty:

- **In boys**, higher testosterone levels cause the larynx and vocal cords to enlarge more. The thyroid cartilage also becomes more prominent, creating a larger Adam’s apple.
- **In girls**, the larynx also grows, but usually less dramatically, so the bump is often smaller or less visible.

This growth also explains why many boys’ voices **deepen during puberty**: a larger larynx and longer, thicker vocal cords vibrate at a lower pitch.

Importantly, **everyone has thyroid cartilage**, so everyone technically has an Adam’s apple — it’s just usually more noticeable in men.
